definitions.explanation: The darkening or reddening of skin from exposure to sunlight. Used both for desirable tanning and painful sunburn.
Discoloration or deterioration of materials such as books, fabric, or furniture caused by prolonged exposure to sunlight.

examples.japanese: {海|うみ}で{日焼|ひや}けしすぎて{痛|いた}い。
examples.english: I got too much sun at the beach and it hurts.

examples.japanese: {日焼|ひや}け{止|ど}めを{塗|ぬ}らないと{肌|はだ}が{真|ま}っ{赤|か}になるよ。
examples.english: If you don't put on sunscreen, your skin will turn bright red.

examples.japanese: {本|ほん}が{日焼|ひや}けしている。
カーテンが{日焼|ひや}けして{色|いろ}が{褪|あ}せた。
examples.english: The curtains faded from sun exposure.

examples.japanese: {古本|ふるほん}は{日焼|ひや}けで{表紙|ひょうし}が{変色|へんしょく}していることが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Used books often have covers discolored from sun exposure.

notes:
USAGE:
{日焼|ひや}け is used both as a noun ({日焼|ひや}けがひどい, the sunburn is bad) and with する as a verb ({日焼|ひや}けする, to get sunburned/tanned). The word covers both the desirable effect of tanning and the undesirable effect of sunburn — context determines which meaning applies.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {日焼|ひや}け{止|ど}め (sunscreen)
- {日焼|ひや}けサロン (tanning salon)
- {日焼|ひや}け{跡|あと} (tan lines)
- {日焼|ひや}けした{肌|はだ} (tanned skin)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{日差|ひざ}し refers to sunlight itself, while {日焼|ひや}け refers to the effect of sun exposure on skin or materials.
